name: בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר
summary: The last king of Babylon in Daniel, who drank from the vessels taken from the house of God in Jerusalem while praising gods of gold and silver, saw the hand write on the wall, and was killed that night when Babylon fell to the Medes and Persians (Dan 5:1–30); Daniel's visions of the four beasts and of the ram and goat are dated by his years (Dan 7:1; 8:1). The name is Akkadian Bēl-šarra-uṣur, “Bel, guard the king”: bēl “lord” (the god Bel), šarru “king”, and uṣur “guard!”. Scripture does not explain it, but the night of his death answers it.

evidence.note: “בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר the king made a great feast for a thousand of his lords.”
The vessels of the house of God; “they praised the gods of gold and silver”.
“You have not humbled your heart … the God in whose hand is your breath you have not glorified.”
“In that night בֵּלְאשַׁצַּר the king of the Chaldeans was killed.”
“In the third year of the reign of Belshazzar the king.”

note: Keys: b.ci.aw (the spelling בֵּלְאשַׁצַּר, Dan 5:30; 8:1) and xb.ah.ad (the Aramaic בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר of Dan 5 and 7); b.bz.ac is a cross-reference. If the two keys count the same tokens twice, name one. Not Belteshazzar (בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר), Daniel's Babylonian name, which Nebuchadnezzar says was “after the name of my god” (Dan 4:5) but is not spelled with בֵּל + שַׁר alone; it is left for its own entry. The Akkadian analysis rests on the cuneiform glossary for each part; no Babylonian record of the king's name was consulted here.
